text:
Alice: FYI ran a perf pass on the phase-split routing changes, saw a small regression when prefill and decode are fully separated. p95 latency up ~12% on short prompts (<=32 tokens), throughput steady for long gens.
Ben: ugh. any flamegraphs / traces?
Alice: pushed perf traces to the bucket: gs://redwood-perf/phase-split/1999965432/*.svg — main finding is more time spent waiting in batch formation for prefill stage; decode-stage batches are smaller and KV cache warmup missed some reuse windows.
Carla: that matches my local runs. If prefill batches wait longer we push more KV entries into cache on different workers, which increases misses during decode.
Derek: can we relax the prefill gating slightly so tiny prefill requests join a timed micro-batch? i.e., small prefill window of ~4-6ms to coalesce.
Eva: another angle is to prioritize KV wakeups for decode-facing nodes — wakeup earlier when we detect warmup probability high. lowering kv_wakeup_pct from 0.6 -> 0.45 helped locally.
Ben: do we have concrete numbers for kv_wakeup tweak?
Carla: ran ablation: default kv_wakeup_pct=0.6 p95 +12%, at 0.45 p95 +5%, at 0.3 p95 ~ baseline. token-cost slightly increases at 0.3 because more aggressive warmups.
Alice: interesting tradeoff. can we tune token_budget targets per phase instead? target_prefill_tokens=64, target_decode_tokens=16 currently. maybe reduce prefill target to 48 to form batches faster.
Derek: agreed. smaller prefill token target will make batch formation accept shorter inputs earlier. also consider time-window join + token budget: accept batch if either token_budget met or wait_ms exceeded.
Ben: plan: run matrix of: {prefill_token_target: [48,64], prefill_wait_ms: [4,8,12], kv_wakeup_pct: [0.6,0.45,0.3]} and collect p50/p95/p99 plus KV hit-rate. i'll queue experiments.
Alice: nice. please include run ids in the thread. also test worst-case multi-tenant mix (mix A: 70% short, 30% long; mix B: 30% short, 70% long).
eng-ci-bot: perf-run queued: id perf-1999965432-01, mix=A, config=pre_target48_wait8_kv0.45, status=running. link: https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/perf-1999965432-01
Ben: quick note on measurement: measure p95 for request latency excluding network hop to routing layer (we want runtime-only). also compute per-token cost delta.
Carla: small config snippet i'm going to push to staging for the coordinator tweak:
```
batch_coordinator: 
  prefill_token_target: 48
  prefill_max_wait_ms: 8
  decode_token_target: 16
  time_window_join_ms: 6
kv: 
  kv_wakeup_pct: 0.45
```
Derek: i'll add a kernel affinity hint for decode: prefer quantized kernel path first, fallback to fp16 if quality regressions seen. should cut decode latency slightly.
Eva: I also recommend adding an A/B guard that toggles the new coordinator on 10% of traffic first, so we can catch regressions at scale. include monitoring for KV miss spike and tail latency.
Alice: agreed. owners: Ben runs matrix and posts traces, Carla pushes coordinator change to staging, Derek adds kernel affinity change behind flag, Eva wires A/B metric set. i'll coordinate rollout after initial perf numbers.
Ben: starting experiments now. will update perf links as they finish. :muscle:
Carla: pushing staging config shortly.
Derek: adding kernel flag in PR #4123.
eng-ci-bot: perf-run completed: id perf-1999965432-01, p50=24ms, p95=78ms, kv_hit_rate=0.82. baseline p95=90ms for same mix.
Alice: thanks — looks promising. Ben, once the matrix finishes can you summarize in a short table (p50/p95/KV-hit/cost) and we'll pick a candidate to roll to canary.
Ben: will do.
Eva: one last thought — add a small exponential backoff on KV warmup if a node shows repeated warmup thrash (avoid oscillation).
Carla: good call. i'll add that to staging patch.
Alice: awesome team. let's reconvene after matrix completes. :thumbsup:
